en: I bought these while looking for black sneakers to wear at the gym. I used to wear running shoes even for weight training, but they felt way too soft under my feet during leg workouts, so I was looking for something else. I usually wear 275 in Nike and 270 in New Balance, and I ordered 270. There's a little extra room in the length. I like how firm they feel underfoot when I squat, and they were fine for about 15 minutes of running on the treadmill after my workout too. I did have to tighten the laces a bit over the top of my foot to feel secure, though. I'm happy with the design—the all-black look is clean.

I used to wear running shoes for leg workouts, but they had a lot of cushioning, so my feet felt a little unstable during squats. But wearing Converse made it uncomfortable to use the treadmill after my workout, so I switched between two pairs of shoes. I'd been looking into DARIMATI shoes for a while, and when I heard a black model was coming out, I waited for preorders to open and ordered a pair. I've worn them for about 2 weeks. I usually wear 280 in Nike and 280 in ASICS, and my feet are slightly wide, so I went with 280 in these too. There's a little extra room in the length, and they fit well over the top of my foot. They're not overly soft underfoot and the grip is decent, so I've been happy with them for squats and leg presses. I tried running on the treadmill at around speed 8 for 20 minutes, and they weren't particularly uncomfortable. I'm still not sure if they're suitable for long-distance running, though. Personally, I think they're a good fit for people who mainly lift weights but also do cardio.

My feet get so sweaty, so when I saw they'd improved the breathability, I waited for preorders and bought them lol. Got them for F45 and so far they seem light and pretty good?? 260 fits perfectly and they're not tight across the width either. Glad they're black since I think dirt will show less haha

I wore these as soon as they arrived, on a day when I got really sweaty in circuit class. They were fine during the workout, but I set them out to dry as soon as I got home. The dark color makes them pretty easy to care for. I figured all-black shoes were pretty much alike, so I went in without high expectations. But they look quite different with workout pants that end at the ankle versus wide-leg sweatpants. There aren't many decorative details, so they don't look overdone, and they worked fine for heading straight out to meet people after a workout. On the other hand, if you're expecting the feel of bright, lightweight running shoes, these might not be your thing. Next time I pick a pair, I'll try to judge them by how they feel after a week of use rather than how they feel when I first put them on.
I already have plenty of black sneakers, but I picked these because the side profile looked different.
Think I'll get a lot of wear out of these
Waited a long time, but I like them.
I hate when the soles feel wobbly during lower-body workouts, but these made it easy to stay focused through the end of today's workout. Like them even more because they're black

I went for a walk at lunch and hit the gym in the evening without bringing a separate pair of shoes. Performance matters, but lately that practicality is what I'm happiest with. When I'm only training my lower body, I prioritize how supported my feet feel, and on days with lots of cardio, I reach for different shoes. So this time I mostly wore these on days when I mixed different types of training. They were fine for short runs and changes of direction, and I could adjust the laces when I wanted to keep my feet firmly in place. Since they're black, they're easy to wear out before and after a workout too. I'm writing this because these were the things I wanted to know about. Of course, what feels right will be different for everyone.

After I switched shoes at the gym, a friend asked what I was wearing haha. I didn't think anyone would notice, but I guess the shape looks a little different. Sometimes I go to a sports field on weekends, and on weekdays I just do short workouts at a gym near home. I've found that how clean the floor is and how much I'm moving around affect how the shoes feel more than the type of exercise does. I should also mention that I haven't tried them enough in intense training yet haha

I have wide feet, so I usually wear 280 in sneakers. My feet are about 275 long, so I always have a hard time choosing a size. I like that the black model has enough room up front that my toes don't get squished. There is a little extra length, though, so I tie the laces tightly when I work out. I've mainly used them for leg presses and squats at the gym, and I've been happy with them because they're not overly soft underfoot. I've also done some easy walking on the treadmill, but I haven't used them for long-distance running yet. Switching between two pairs of shoes was a hassle for me, so being able to do everything with one pair is what I like most.

Bought these for CrossFit lol. Saw the black ones were coming out, waited, and ordered them, and they're really easy to wear and look great!! I've tried burpees and box jumps in them, and my feet feel secure. They're more on the firm, sturdy side than super light? I've only worn them a few times so I'll have to see how they go, but I'm happy so far haha

I have high insteps, so I usually go up a size in shoes. My usual size is 265, but I bought 270 because of my wide feet. I'd been waiting since I heard the black ones were coming out, and I ordered them with a preorder discount. They're roomy and comfortable across the width, but there's a lot more extra length than I expected. But I think 260 would be too small, so it's a shame there's no 265. I tried working out in them, and they feel nice and firm underfoot. I like the design too. I just wish there were a few more size options.

I bought these after seeing the new release on Instagram. I usually wear 275 in Nike and 270 in New Balance, but I have wide feet, so I spent a bit of time deciding on a size. I got 270, and there's some room up front. I've tried both squats and the treadmill at the gym, and they work fine for both. Personally, I think the black looks really clean lol

I started going to the gym about 6 months ago, and I'd just been wearing running shoes lol. My feet kept feeling like they were sinking into the cushioning on leg days, so I was looking for gym shoes when I heard preorders were opening for the new black ones and waited!! I wear 275 but bought 270, and they fit perfectly. They're fine for squats, and I had no issues with about 20 minutes on the treadmill either. Changing shoes was a hassle, so that's the best part lol
